items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: some of the stuff I played with Billy Cobham’s band was tremendous fun

ctx.x: Well of all the groups I guess of those groups, the most colorful, the most musical, the most interesting. For a short period or a period, especially when I started playing the guitar synthesizer I kind always looked to Zawinul as kind of a role model. And since I was playing with Peter Erskine who had played with Weather Report, you know he would always give me some insight into how Joe would do something or how he thought about things. And it’s interesting. He’s a very creative man. He’s one of the only people…

it would be Weather Report and the Mahavishnu Orchestra that had completely different approaches to playing that kind of music, and of course Miles’ bands. But I thought most of the other stuff that I would hear, including the stuff that I was involved in, not that it was bad, I mean some of the stuff I played with Billy Cobham’s band was tremendous fun and I think some of it was quite good, but I think a lot of the music out there was just, after a while I think it was just people were just trying to make money.…

One more little quote I was curious about here, you weren’t talking about yourself I don’t think, but you’ve noticed a syndrome that some people have where they feel guilty about being a great musician? Do you remember saying that?
